policy_title: Negotiate New Trade Agreements and Sector Deals
stated: Labour will pursue targeted trade agreements aligned with its industrial strategy and economic strengths, aiming to expand markets for British exporters and attract foreign direct investment. They will publish a trade strategy and seek standalone sector deals (e.g., digital, mutual recognition agreements for services) to promote exports. The party will also lead international discussions to modernise trade rules through the WTO and CPTPP.

source.quote: Labour will seek targeted trade agreements aligned with our industrial strategy and economic strengths, to bring prosperity to communities across England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland. We will publish a trade strategy and use every lever available to get UK business the access it needs to international markets. This will promote the highest standards when it comes to food production. As well as striking new free trade agreements, Labour will seek to negotiate standalone sector deals, such as digital, or mutual recognition agreements, to promote our services exports. We will lead international discussions to modernise trade rules and agreements so they work for Britain, promoting deeper trade and co-operation including through the World Trade Organisation and the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership.

bearing_set.reason: Expanding export markets, attracting FDI and sector deals (digital, services) are directly targeted at job creation, wage growth, and employment quality in those industries — a real, contestable verdict on good work and fair pay.

Expanding export markets, attracting FDI, and securing sector deals (digital, services, MRAs) directly affect real living standards, productivity, business investment and economic opportunity — O13's core indicators.

membership_note: O13 is the primary target of the policy; O4 is a genuine secondary bearing because sector-specific deals and FDI attraction materially affect job creation and wage levels in the targeted industries. Other fundamentals (O2, O12, O14) are too indirect at this high-level negotiating/strategy stage to clear the non-negligible bar without knowing the specific deals struck.
